name: Thidranki
summary: The oldest of the proving fields, a lost farmstead of tomte and bwca around Thidranki Faste, the one field whose renegades were driven out (20-24).

facts.text: Thidranki is the battleground for levels 20 to 24 (region 252); level is the only limit in Offline DAoC.
Its central keep is Thidranki Faste; an Albion, a Midgard and a Hibernia portal keep stand at the same three places as in the other battlegrounds.
Thidranki Faste starts neutral in the release world.
Thidranki, Murdaigean and Caledonia were the classic battlegrounds; Abermenai came with patch 1.62 (June 2003).

Its monsters are tomte hunters, soldiers, mystics and visionaries, perturbed bwca, mature boars, rabid and maddened badgers and clicking beetles (levels 19-24). Haluka (24) is a bwca twice the size of the others, by the Hibernia portal keep, and does not wander; the other bwca roam.

facts.text: Thidranki has no Renegade Chieftain or renegade camp in the world data, unlike Abermenai, Murdaigean and Caledon.

facts.text: Each portal keep has named siegemasters: Salendar and Cadman (Albion), Ordrand and Sigfreid (Midgard), Camey and Erinden (Hibernia); Void Merchants trade realm points at the Midgard and Hibernia portal keeps.

facts.text: In the Old Norse tale Þiðranda þáttr ok Þórhalls, the young Thidrandi is killed on a winter night by nine women in black, the disir of the old faith. Thidranki may echo the name; to verify.
Tomte are the farm spirits of Swedish folklore and bwca the household spirits of Welsh tradition; both are the spirits of a farmstead.
The farm, the feud of the two kinds of farm spirit and the Faste Winter are Living Server lore.

story:
Thidranki is the oldest of the proving fields, and before it was a field it was a farm.

The farm. The skalds of Mularn say a northman called Thidrand cleared the ground in the old days and built a longhouse where the Faste now stands, and kept cattle on the hill, and that the farm took its name from him. The bards of the west say the ground was cleared long before by people of their own and that the northman only moved in. Both are probably true, because the farm had two kinds of spirit, and a farm only gets its spirits from the people who keep it. The tomte came with the northmen: small, grey and grave, who mind the beasts and punish a careless farmer. The bwca came with the older folk: shaggy house-spirits who do the work at night for a bowl of cream and turn on a household that forgets them. For as long as the farm stood they kept it together, and quarrelled, and kept it.

What went wrong. The farm did not survive the realm wars. Nobody agrees on how it ended: Midgard says a winter took the household, Hibernia says reavers from the south did, and Albion says it does not remember the farm at all. What is agreed is that the household died or left, and the spirits did not. A tomte without a farmer and a bwca without a bowl of cream are both very angry things, and each kind blamed the other. When the realms came to the hill in the first summer of the fields they found a ruin, a stone keep built by somebody over the longhouse, renegades in the keep, and the tomte and the bwca fighting each other across the fields for a farm that was no longer there.

The Faste Winter. Thidranki was the first field the realms sent their young to, and the first they fought over hard. In the second winter of the fields all three realms marched on the Faste in the same week, each without knowing the others were coming, and the renegades who held it found themselves under three sieges at once. They left. Their chieftain walked out of the back gate in the snow with whoever would follow and went south and east to the wood of Murdaigean, where, the renegades say, he took that keep's name instead. Thidranki Faste has had no renegade lord since. It belongs to whichever realm last took it, and its walls have changed colour more often than any keep in the world.

What lives there now. The tomte still hunt and soldier across the hill, and their mystics and visionaries still watch the sky for the farmer who will not come. The bwca roam, perturbed, and their eldest, Haluka, who is twice the size of any of them and remembers the farm when it had a fire, keeps to one place by the Hibernian portal keep and does not leave it. The boars and badgers of the old fields have gone wild and mean. At each portal keep the realms keep siegemasters, Salendar and Cadman for Albion, Ordrand and Sigfreid for Midgard, Camey and Erinden for Hibernia, because Thidranki is the field where the young first learn that a keep can be taken.

Why it matters. Every veteran of every realm remembers Thidranki. It is where the realms learned to send their young to a field instead of the frontier, and where the young learned that a keep belongs to whoever is standing in it.
legend: Thidranki is the 20-24 battleground and the busiest of the four: the classic one, where most characters first fight over a keep that matters. Thidranki Faste in the middle has no renegade chieftain here; it is whoever's took it last, so it changes hands a lot. The siegemasters at each portal keep (Salendar and Cadman for Albion, Ordrand and Sigfreid for Midgard, Camey and Erinden for Hibernia) sell rams and the like, and there are Void Merchants at the Midgard and Hibernia portal keeps. The tomte and the bwca aggro on anyone, and the bwca wander, so watch your back when you rest out in the fields. Haluka, the big bwca by the Hibernian portal keep, is level 24 and twice the size of the others; Hibernians meet him on their first day. Players call the field Thid and swear it was better in the old days.

firstEntry: A hill of old fields, gone wild. A keep stands on top.
Small grey figures watch from the long grass.
Somewhere a bwca is muttering about cream.
This was a farm once. The ground remembers the plough.

areas.name: Thidranki Faste
lines: The Faste is built over an old longhouse.
No renegade lord holds this keep. It is anyone's.
The walls have changed colour many times.

Albion's portal keep, on the southern slope.

areas.name: Midgard portal keep
lines: Ordrand and Sigfreid keep Midgard's siege gear.
A tomte watches Midgard's gate. It looks disappointed.

areas.name: Hibernia portal keep
lines: Camey and Erinden keep Hibernia's siege gear.
Hibernia's portal keep. Bwca country starts here.

areas.name: Haluka's corner
lines: An old bwca, bigger than the rest, will not move from here.
Haluka remembers the farm. He is still waiting for cream.

loremaster.intro: Thidranki? The oldest of the [proving fields], and a [farm] before it was a field. Its spirits are still there, the [tomte] and the [bwca], and the eldest of the bwca, [Haluka], still waits for his cream. The renegades were driven out in the [Faste Winter], and [Thidranki Faste] has had no lord of its own since. Ask me about the [siegemasters], too, if you mean to take it.

topics.proving fields: The four contested fields away from the great frontier where the realms send soldiers of one age at a time: Abermenai, [Thidranki], Murdaigean and Caledon. Thidranki was the first.
topics.thidranki: The field of 20 to 24, a farm before the realm wars, named, the skalds say, for a northman called Thidrand who cleared it. Its keep is [Thidranki Faste].
topics.farm: A longhouse on a hill with cattle and two kinds of spirit, the [tomte] of the northmen and the [bwca] of the older folk. The household died or left in the realm wars; Midgard says a winter took it, Hibernia a raid, and Albion does not remember it at all.
topics.tomte: Small grey farm spirits of the north who mind the beasts and punish a careless farmer. With no farmer left they hunt and soldier across the hill, and their visionaries watch the sky for one.
topics.bwca: Shaggy house-spirits of the older folk who do a farm's work at night for a bowl of cream and turn on a household that forgets them. Thidranki's are perturbed, and roam. Their eldest is [Haluka].
topics.haluka: The eldest bwca of Thidranki, twice the size of any other, who remembers the [farm] when it had a fire. He keeps to one place near the Hibernian portal keep and does not leave it. He is still waiting for his cream, and he is not friendly.
topics.faste winter: The second winter of the fields, when all three realms marched on [Thidranki Faste] in the same week without knowing the others were coming. The renegades left by the back gate in the snow, and their chieftain went to Murdaigean and took that keep's name.
topics.thidranki faste: A stone keep built over the old longhouse. Since the [Faste Winter] it has had no renegade lord and belongs to whichever realm last took it.
topics.siegemasters: Each realm keeps siegemasters at its Thidranki portal keep: Salendar and Cadman for Albion, Ordrand and Sigfreid for Midgard, Camey and Erinden for Hibernia. Thidranki is where the young first learn that a keep can be taken.

book.title: The Farm under the Faste, by Ulfhild Long-Memory, skald of Mularn
pages: I am a skald of Mularn and I have sung the farm of Thidrand at three funerals, so I will set it down before I forget a verse. Thidrand was a young man of the north who came south and west over the water and cleared a hill nobody wanted. He built a longhouse of turf and timber and kept cattle, and the tomte came with him in his ship, as they come with every northman who keeps beasts. When he turned the first sod he found a bowl of cream already set out on a stone, and nobody to have set it, and he did not drink it. That was wise of him.

The bowl was for the bwca, the old folk's house-spirits, who were on the hill before him. The tomte did not like them and they did not like the tomte, but they both liked the farm, and between them the beasts were minded and the work was done at night and the farmer who forgot either was sorry. Our skalds say Thidrand died young on a winter night, called out of the house by women in black, as in the old tale of his namesake. The bards of the west say reavers took the farm. I have heard both sung and I do not choose.

When our young came to the hill in the first summer of the fields there was a stone keep on the longhouse and men of no realm in it, and the tomte and the bwca were fighting each other in the long grass for a farm that was no longer there. A tomte without a farmer is a sad and dangerous thing. A bwca without his cream is worse. Our recruits learned to sleep with their backs to a wall. In the second winter all three realms came for the keep in the same week, and the renegades went out the back in the snow.

The eldest bwca is called Haluka. He sits near the Hibernians' portal keep and does not move, and he is twice the size of the others, and I am told that he remembers the farm when it had a fire. I went to see him once, with a bowl of cream, because I am a skald and I wanted the verse. He did not take it. He looked at the bowl and then at me, and then he came for me, and I ran. I have made a verse of that too. The cream was the wrong cream, or I was the wrong farmer, or it was simply too late.

albion.story: Albion does not remember the farm and does not much care. Its captains tell Thidranki as the field where Albion's young learned siegecraft: the first ram an Albion squire ever pushed against a keep was pushed up Thidranki's hill, and Siegemaster Salendar's family has kept Albion's siege gear at the southern portal keep since. Albion's squires call the field the Proving Hill and say that the tomte are only goblins with better manners.
albion.legend: Albion players say Thid is where you learn to push a ram, and that every Albion squire's first keep take is the Faste. They also say the bwca hate Albion most, which every realm says about itself.

lore: albs say thidranki is where the first alb squire pushed a ram up a hill. [siegemaster salendar's family|the siegemasters remember]

midgard.story: Midgard claims the farm. The skalds of Mularn sing that Thidrand was a northman and the tomte came over the water in his ship, and that the field still bears his name; they tell the old tale of his namesake who was called out on a winter night by women in black, and say Thidrand of the farm died the same way. Midgard's recruits leave a little porridge out for the tomte before they ride, as their grandmothers did for the farm tomte at home, and say it is only good manners.
midgard.legend: Midgard players leave porridge for the tomte at the portal keep, out of habit. The tomte aggro on them anyway. The skalds say a tomte never forgives a farmer who left, and that every northman is that farmer now.

lore: the skalds say thidrand was a northman and the tomte came over in his ship. [its our farm|thid is a mid name]

hibernia.story: Hibernia's bards say the hill was cleared by people of the west long before any northman came, and that the bwca are the proof, since a bwca only comes to an old house. They say Haluka is the last of the hill's first household and that he waits for cream from the hands that set it out before the realms had names. Hibernia's recruits meet Haluka on their first day, because their portal keep is nearest his corner, and come back with a story.
hibernia.legend: Hibernians say Haluka is theirs, and that every Hibernian recruit is warned about him and goes to look anyway. He is level 24 and does not like visitors. Most Hibernians' first death in Thid is Haluka.

lore: the bards say the bwca prove thid was ours first. [a bwca only comes to an old house|older than the northmen]
